hero.intro: A daemon-first terminal workspace for people whose work spans machines, networks and screens. Keep terminals alive in one pool, then observe and operate them from the TUI or official App.

pool.title: Terminal pool / Build machine
pool.views: Windows, panes and devices are only views.
pool.detail: Detach the TUI. Close the App. Change the layout. The daemon keeps lifecycle and history where the terminal actually runs.

products.title2: Add the App and Cloud when you need reachability.

core.title: Muxvia Core
core.copy: The daemon, CLI and TUI form a terminal workspace built around long-lived terminals rather than disposable panes.

app.title: Muxvia App
app.copy: Carry the same endpoint list in your pocket. Pair with a daemon, reconnect to running work and move files without exposing a web terminal.

cloud.title: Muxvia Cloud
cloud.copy: The official cloud service for Muxvia handles device discovery, signaling and managed Relay when changing networks cannot connect directly.

products.boundary: Muxvia Cloud and the official mobile App are proprietary Muxvia products. The open-source Go core remains fully usable with local and SSH endpoints without a cloud account.

items.title: Persistent terminal pool
items.copy: Terminals live in the daemon, independent of the pane or window currently showing them.

items.title: Authoritative history
items.copy: Reconnect to the same lifecycle, live surface and history instead of rebuilding context from a local scrollback.

items.title: Local, SSH and WebRTC
items.copy: One endpoint model reaches local machines, SSH daemons and managed cloud devices without changing terminal identity.

items.title: Files beside the terminal
items.copy: Browse, preview, upload and download files through the same authorized protocol session.

connectivity.copy: Muxvia Cloud gets the client and daemon to the same encrypted session. It does not receive terminal capability grants, commands, history, file metadata or terminal payload.
connectivity.pathShown: Actual direct or Relay path shown
connectivity.truth: Terminal truth remains on the daemon

plans.copy: Local, SSH, multi-endpoint workspaces and terminal capability remain part of the open core. Plans fund official discovery, Relay capacity and account services.

managed-free.name: Managed Free
managed-free.description: Official device discovery and managed signaling for personal endpoints.

pro.name: Pro
pro.description: Managed Relay capacity and route intelligence for people who work across networks.

team.name: Team
team.description: Organization controls and auditable endpoint access without moving terminal truth to the cloud.

login.copy: Reach registered machines and manage cloud services without exposing terminal authorization.
login.controlTitle: Manage connectivity without moving terminal trust into the cloud.
login.controlCopy: The Controller stores account, subscription, quota and topology metadata. Terminal grants and payload remain end to end between your devices.
login.intro: Sign in to manage nodes, subscriptions, account settings, and referral rewards.
login.credentials: Credentials are never returned to page JavaScript.
login.session: HttpOnly session / SameSite Strict / CSRF protected

device.enterCopy: Enter the short code shown in the Muxvia App or TUI. Your password and browser session stay on this website.
device.title: Approve this Muxvia client
device.copy: Check the device and code before approving. This grants cloud connectivity only; terminal permissions remain daemon-owned.
device.waitingForDevice: Waiting for the phone to scan this QR code...
device.error: This device request is invalid, expired, or already used.
device.approvedCopy: You can return to Muxvia. The client will finish signing in without receiving your password or browser session.

controls.unlocked: Destructive controls are available for 5 minutes
controls.required: Required only when removing or disconnecting a device

overview.proof: Terminal authorization stays end to end. Cloud services only manage connectivity.

nodes.mobileCopy: Create a short-lived QR code, scan it in the Muxvia App, then review the phone details before approving it.
nodes.qrAlt: One-time QR code for activating the Muxvia mobile app
nodes.scanCopy: In the Muxvia App, open Settings and choose Scan QR from web.
nodes.approvedCopy: The phone is finishing activation. This code cannot authorize another device.
nodes.activationError: This activation could not be completed. Create a new code and try again.
nodes.activationExpired: This QR code has expired. Create a new one to continue.
nodes.daemonNote: Muxvia daemons run terminal and file services. These are the servers that the App, TUI, and desktop GUI connect to.
nodes.clientNote: Phones, TUI sessions, and desktop GUIs authorized for Muxvia Cloud appear here. Clients are not servers and never belong in the App machine list.
nodes.enrollmentCommand: Run on the server: muxvia cloud enroll {{code}}
nodes.noDaemons: No daemon servers are enrolled yet.

daemonFlow.title: Add a daemon
daemonFlow.intro: Create a ten-minute code, run it on the daemon host, then review and approve the submitted device identity here.
daemonFlow.waiting: Waiting for the daemon to submit its public identity.
daemonFlow.approved: Approved. The daemon is completing its identity proof and this code cannot be reused.
daemonFlow.createError: Could not create daemon login code

mobileFlow.renderError: Could not render activation QR code

billing.included: Direct connectivity and managed signaling included.

enrollmentUx.reenrollNote: A removed daemon can be enrolled again without deleting its local device identity. A new code replaces any unused code for this account.
enrollmentUx.copyError: The browser could not copy the command. Select the command text manually.
enrollmentUx.expired: This enrollment code has expired. Generate a new one.
enrollmentUx.error: The enrollment code could not be created. Try again.
